question: does lifting the workforce-2 mining gate (opportunistic MINE emission when a unit is iron-adjacent, has free capacity, the currently-planned worker's IRON bill is unmet, and the unit's own assigned action isn't itself bill-critical) clear the mechanism gates (IRON/game >= 4.0, unmined-reachable-workforce>=2 episodes down >= 50%, worker-3 TRAIN in >= 25% of tasks, no waste-sweep detector worse by > 10%) and value gates (overall + activated-subset mean >= +1.0, CI lower bound >= 0.0, worst family >= -1.0, catastrophes/negative-mass not worse) on a fresh 2,048-task panel vs the exact resident control?

phase_0_preflight.method: 64 tasks, D173b's own already-sealed range 9,854,000-9,854,063, seat 0, resident self-play, unmodified dev copy; play forward to the turn own-workforce first reaches 2, synthetically credit the bank to exactly cover a cheap-helper (1,1,0,1) bill at n=2, continue for up to 10 more turns, check for a TRAIN command in own output
phase_0_preflight.finding: MoisanBot::can_train (yamo_orchard_live.rs:834-845) hard-codes `if n >= 2 { return false }` before ever evaluating affordability -- the live resident cannot train a 3rd worker under any circumstance, independent of bank contents. Distinct from and complementary to D160's documented 'zero affordability windows' finding (a bank-economics fact, not a code-gate fact).
phase_0_preflight.scope_decision: Variant B: both deltas in one cycle, same lineage, same one-site character -- Delta 1 (opportunistic mining, unchanged from the frozen protocol) plus the minimal TRAIN-gate repair (delete the `n >= 2 ||` clause from can_train, deadline guard and affordability check otherwise untouched)

delta_1_opportunistic_mining.architecture: stateless post-selection rewrite of the resident's own already-resolved assigned command (positional zip against a freshly sorted own-unit list, not string-parsing a unit id -- correctly attributes a bare 'WAIT', which carries no id in this engine); called once from commands(), immediately after apply_opponent_crop_harvest_contact and before remember_own_plant_attempts
delta_1_opportunistic_mining.conditions: (a) is_adjacent(iron, unit.cell), the identical check iron_candidates itself uses; (b) unit.free_capacity() > 0; (c) training_cost(own_count, desired.tuple())[IRON] > deposited IRON + IRON carried across all own units; (d) the unit's currently-assigned command is not a DROP while it carries IRON, nor (defensively, unreachable in practice) a PICK ... IRON
delta_1_opportunistic_mining.cross_turn_state: none -- recomputed fresh every call from view/commands/desired

delta_2_train_gate_repair.change: deleted the `n >= 2 ||` clause; the pre-existing `TOTAL_TURNS - view.turn <= 20` deadline guard and the unchanged PLUM/LEMON/APPLE/IRON affordability check are the only remaining logic
untouched: training_affordable (its own internal n>=2 branch is unreachable via enforce_training_deadline's own more restrictive own-count<2 guard, unaffected by this repair)
desired_second selection logic (ensure_opening/choose_second_troll/opening_options), frozen once workforce reaches 2 exactly as before

delta_2_fidelity_gate.sample_method: 40 randomly-sampled activated tasks (fixed seed 174002) out of 1,595; every individual MINE-emission instance attributable to the fix (candidate issues MINE for a unit/turn where control does not) checked against all 4 conditions using candidate's own pre-turn state for (a)/(b)/(c) and control's recorded command as ground truth for (d)

control_snapshot: rust/src/d171a_control_resident_snapshot.rs (reused unmodified; verified same SHA-256 as the dev copy before the fix was applied and again after restore)

panel.seed_range_note: fresh range per protocol (9,855,000-9,855,127); pre-lock grep of both ledger volumes for 9,855 found no prior use; disjoint from D171a (9,853,xxx) and D173a/b (9,854,xxx)

verdict_rule: all mechanism gates AND all value gates pass -> QUALIFIED (build candidate pair, STOP at arena gate, new owner authorization required for promotion); mechanism passes but value fails -> CLOSED-AT-VALUE; mechanism fails -> CLOSED-AT-MECHANISM with the shortfall quantified against the 84.4% counterfactual prediction; integrity failure -> BLOCKED

root_cause_of_mechanism_failure.diagnosis: the live resident's actual TRAIN target (YamoOpeningPolicy::TUNED_CARRY, preferred_min_carry=2) is far pricier than B3.9's synthetic cheap_helper (1,1,0,1) reference: recovered from 1,595 activated candidate games, mean training_cost(n=2, desired) is PLUM=6.23 LEMON=5.87 APPLE=2.00 IRON=7.12. This fix raises IRON acquisition 10.6x (0.51->5.40/game) and clears the IRON leg comfortably, but does nothing for PLUM/LEMON: peak post-workforce-2 bank never reached the PLUM bill in 1595/1595 games (100.0%) and never reached the LEMON bill in 1587/1595 games (99.5%); the dominant shortfall combination (1264/1595 = 79.2%) is PLUM+LEMON short together, IRON alone is essentially never the sole blocker any more. This matches B3.8/B3.9's own prediction that iron credited alone barely moves the needle because fruit remains independently binding -- the 84.4% counterfactual required BOTH slacks credited together against a cheaper synthetic spec than the real desired.
root_cause_of_mechanism_failure.value_interpretation: IRON is not itself a scored resource (score = banked PLUM+LEMON+APPLE+BANANA+4*WOOD); since worker-3 training essentially never completes, every turn diverted to MINE is pure opportunity cost against whatever productive (fruit/wood) action it displaced, with no offsetting benefit -- directly explaining the strongly negative value result across all 8 opponent families.
